# EXPANSION CW133-02 — The List on a Borrowed Pencil

## A prose-first game-content plan grounded in an existing survivor journal entry.

### Prose Wave 133: The Work Between Countdowns

**Content type:** long-form in-game prose bank with four optional literary passes per source focus.

## 1. Expansion thesis

This plan expands attention around the list on a borrowed pencil while leaving the journal row intact. Its center is a medication list rewritten at a cold ridge. The bank offers different distances and registers for rereading the same recorded material; it does not add a new day, memory, event, relationship, quest, or system.

## 2. Story question

What kind of responsibility does the Courier accept when he rewrites a list that belongs to a Surgeon whose hands shook?

## 3. Verified source record

The complete JSON entry below is copied from the current local source. Preserve its id, author_id, author_name, day, hour, knowledge_key, timestamp, and exact text. Candidate prose is editorial material, not part of the loaded row.

```json
{
  "id": "journal_raw_b3_22_courier_the_warehouse_walk",
  "text": "We are at the ridge. Day 1. 14 kilometres. The Veteran walks like he has walked 14 kilometres before, which he has, many times, in a life before this one that he does not talk about. The Mechanic walks like a man carrying a pry bar, which he is. The Hunter walks like a man who is listening to everything, which he is. I walk like a man carrying the Surgeon's list on his hand. I washed the hand at the stream crossing and the names blurred and I re-wrote them at the ridge with the pencil the Teacher gave the Child Soldier, which I borrowed, which I will return. Amoxicillin. Doxycycline. Ciprofloxacin. The names are on my hand and the hand is mine and the list is the Surgeon's and the Surgeon's hands shook when he wrote it. I did not tell him I saw. I will not tell him. The ridge is cold. We will not make a fire. The Hunter says fire is a beacon. The Veteran says fire is a beacon. The Mechanic says fire is warm. The Mechanic is outvoted. We sleep cold. I have the hand-crank radio. I will listen to 149.0 before I sleep. If the bunker is there, I will hear the carrier. If the bunker is there, they will hear nothing, because I am not transmitting. I am listening. Listening is the thing I can do from the ridge. The warehouse is tomorrow. The Surgeon's list is on my hand. The hand is steady. The hands that wrote it were not. I will be the steady hand for him. That is the job the Surgeon gave me. I did not know that was the job until I wrote it here.",
  "timestamp": "Day 183, 22h",
  "author_name": "The Courier",
  "author_id": "the_courier",
  "knowledge_key": "courier_warehouse_walk_surgeons_list",
  "day": 183,
  "hour": 22.0
}
```

## 4. Fixed canon and open space

On Day 1 at the ridge, the Courier has walked fourteen kilometres, washed the medication names from his hand, and rewritten them with the pencil borrowed from the Child Soldier. The team will not make a fire; the Courier listens on a hand-crank radio at 149.0 and does not transmit. The warehouse is tomorrow. Do not report what they find there. Candidate language may add an image, rhythm, or private impression as an editorial draft, but no proposed addition becomes a further remembered event or confirmed fact until the existing content owner selects and reviews it against the source.

## 5. Human center

The source voice is The Courier. The Courier’s young, practical voice turns the physical list into a promise to stay steady for someone else. Keep listening distinct from transmitting, and return the borrowed pencil rather than making it his. The prose may notice what the author can count, hear, repair, fear, or leave uncertain, while keeping the account’s limits visible.
